in_greek.name: Λεωνέλ

in_latin.name: Leonel
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Leonel derivatur ex nomine Leonis qui est leo et filius. Nomen significat 'filium leonis' et refertur ad fortitudinem et animositatem quae sunt virtutes christianae.

Leonel, the son of a Breton count, is said to have been evangelized by Saint Malo. He was a monk at the Abbey of Redon and later became the bishop of Nantes. Leonel was imprisoned in Angers by the Frankish king Childebert I and died as a martyr in prison.
